topicName: Compute Engine: Custom Images, Startup Scripts, Metadata
content:
[{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Compute Engine: Custom Images, Startup Scripts, and Metadata"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"This tutorial covers creating custom images, using startup scripts, and leveraging metadata within Google Compute Engine (GCE). These features are essential for automating instance configuration and management."},{"order":3,"type":"subheading","text":"Custom Images"},{"order":4,"type":"paragraph","text":"Custom images allow you to create a template of a virtual machine's (VM) disk. This is useful for deploying pre-configured environments, ensuring consistency across instances, and capturing the state of a VM for backup or disaster recovery."},{"order":5,"type":"subheading","text":"Creating a Custom Image"},{"order":6,"type":"paragraph","text":"There are several ways to create a custom image:"},{"order":7,"type":"bullet_point","text":"From a disk: Create an image directly from an existing persistent disk."},{"order":8,"type":"bullet_point","text":"From a snapshot: Create an image from a snapshot of a persistent disk."},{"order":9,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Import an image: Import a virtual disk image from your local machine or Cloud Storage."},{"order":10,"type":"paragraph","text":"Here's how to create a custom image from a disk using the gcloud CLI:"},{"order":11,"type":"code","text":"gcloud compute images create [IMAGE_NAME] --source-disk [DISK_NAME] --source-disk-zone [DISK_ZONE]"},{"order":12,"type":"paragraph","text":"Replace [IMAGE_NAME] with the desired name for your image, [DISK_NAME] with the name of the disk you want to create the image from, and [DISK_ZONE] with the zone where the disk is located."},{"order":13,"type":"subheading","text":"Startup Scripts"},{"order":14,"type":"paragraph","text":"Startup scripts are scripts that run automatically when a Compute Engine instance starts. They are commonly used to install software, configure settings, and perform other initialization tasks."},{"order":15,"type":"subheading","text":"Using Startup Scripts"},{"order":16,"type":"paragraph","text":"You can specify a startup script when creating a new instance or updating an existing one. The script can be provided as a file or directly as a string."},{"order":17,"type":"paragraph","text":"Here's an example of creating an instance with a startup script that installs the Apache web server:"},{"order":18,"type":"code","text":"gcloud compute instances create [INSTANCE_NAME] --image-family [IMAGE_FAMILY] --image-project [IMAGE_PROJECT] --metadata startup-script=\"#! /bin/bash\\napt-get update\\napt-get install -y apache2\\necho '

Hello, world!

' > /var/www/html/index.html\""},{"order":19,"type":"paragraph","text":"Replace [INSTANCE_NAME] with the name of your instance, [IMAGE_FAMILY] with the desired image family (e.g., 'debian-10'), and [IMAGE_PROJECT] with the image project (e.g., 'debian-cloud'). Note the escaped newline characters '\\n' within the script."},{"order":20,"type":"paragraph","text":"Alternatively, you can provide the startup script in a file:"},{"order":21,"type":"code","text":"gcloud compute instances create [INSTANCE_NAME] --image-family [IMAGE_FAMILY] --image-project [IMAGE_PROJECT] --metadata-from-file startup-script=[SCRIPT_FILE]"},{"order":22,"type":"paragraph","text":"Replace [SCRIPT_FILE] with the path to your startup script file."},{"order":23,"type":"subheading","text":"Metadata"},{"order":24,"type":"paragraph","text":"Metadata is information about a Compute Engine instance that can be accessed from within the instance itself. This includes information like the instance name, zone, project ID, and custom metadata that you define."},{"order":25,"type":"subheading","text":"Accessing Metadata"},{"order":26,"type":"paragraph","text":"You can access metadata using the metadata server, which is available at a specific IP address (169.254.169.254) from within the instance. You can use curl to retrieve metadata."},{"order":27,"type":"code","text":"curl http://metadata.google.internal/computeMetadata/v1/instance/zone -H \"Metadata-Flavor: Google\""},{"order":28,"type":"paragraph","text":"The \"Metadata-Flavor: Google\" header is required for accessing the metadata server."},{"order":29,"type":"subheading","text":"Custom Metadata"},{"order":30,"type":"paragraph","text":"You can also define your own custom metadata when creating or updating an instance. This can be useful for passing configuration information to your applications."},{"order":31,"type":"code","text":"gcloud compute instances create [INSTANCE_NAME] --image-family [IMAGE_FAMILY] --image-project [IMAGE_PROJECT] --metadata my-key=\"my-value\""},{"order":32,"type":"paragraph","text":"To retrieve custom metadata from within the instance:"},{"order":33,"type":"code","text":"curl http://metadata.google.internal/computeMetadata/v1/instance/attributes/my-key -H \"Metadata-Flavor: Google\""},{"order":34,"type":"subheading","text":"Conclusion"},{"order":35,"type":"paragraph","text":"Custom images, startup scripts, and metadata are powerful tools for managing and configuring Compute Engine instances. By using these features, you can automate deployments, ensure consistency, and pass configuration information to your applications."}]
